title: Descent of the immersion to a finite stage
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] which is
everywhere quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], with $S$
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $\nu_f:N_f\to S$ be the
relative normalization of $S$ in $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], with $X\xrightarrow{\iota_f} N_f$ a quasi-compact open immersion [pqf-lem-normalization-open], and let
$N_f=\varprojlim_\lambda T_\lambda$, with projections $p_\lambda:N_f\to T_\lambda$, be the presentation of $N_f$ as a
filtered limit of finite $S$-schemes, with affine transition maps,
supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-morphism-limit-of-finite]. Then
there are an index $\lambda_0$ and a factorization

$$
X\xrightarrow{\ j\ }T\xrightarrow{\ i\ }T_{\lambda_0}
$$

of $p_{\lambda_0}\circ\iota_f$, i.e. $i\circ j=p_{\lambda_0}\circ\iota_f$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $i$ a closed immersion.
If moreover $S$ is
locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] — in particular if
$f$ is locally of finite presentation over a locally Noetherian
$S$ — the index $\lambda_0$ may be chosen so that
$T_{\lambda_0}$ is finite and of finite presentation over $S$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-morphism-limit-of-finite], $N_f$ is a filtered limit of finite $S$-schemes $T_\lambda$ with affine transition maps. A finite morphism is affine, hence quasi-compact and separated (Stacks Tag 01S7), so by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2) each $T_\lambda$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $S$ being so. By [pqf-lem-normalization-open], $\iota_f:X\to N_f$ is an open immersion; $f$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $S$ is quasi-compact, so $X$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2), and hence so is its image $V=\iota_f(X)\cong X$, a quasi-compact open of $N_f$. Clause (1) of [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] gives an index $\lambda_1$ and a quasi-compact open $U_{\lambda_1}\subset T_{\lambda_1}$ with $p_{\lambda_1}^{-1}(U_{\lambda_1})=V$. Letting $U_\lambda$ be its preimage in $T_\lambda$ for $\lambda\ge\lambda_1$, clause (3) of that lemma identifies $V$ with the filtered limit of the quasi-compact $U_\lambda$, with affine transition maps.

The open immersion $\iota_f$ induces an isomorphism $X\to V$, in particular a closed immersion of $S$-schemes into the filtered limit $V=\varprojlim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_1}U_\lambda$, whose transition maps are affine and whose stages $U_\lambda$ are quasi-compact (Step 1). The structure morphism $X\to S$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. [pqf-lem-limit-immersion-descends] therefore gives an index $\lambda_0\ge\lambda_1$ for which the composite $X\to V\to U_{\lambda_0}$, the corestriction of $p_{\lambda_0}\circ\iota_f$, is a closed immersion.

Let $h=p_{\lambda_0}\circ\iota_f:X\to U_{\lambda_0}\hookrightarrow T_{\lambda_0}$. It is a closed immersion followed by an open immersion, hence an immersion [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Since $X$ is quasi-compact (Step 1) and $T_{\lambda_0}$ is quasi-separated (Step 1), $h$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1). [lem-pqf-qc-immersion-open-closed-factor] gives $X\xrightarrow{j}T\xrightarrow{i}T_{\lambda_0}$ with $j$ an open immersion, $i$ a closed immersion and $i\circ j=h=p_{\lambda_0}\circ\iota_f$. A closed immersion is quasi-separated (indeed separated), so $T$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2), $T_{\lambda_0}$ being so; as $X$ is quasi-compact, $j$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1).

If $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], the finite morphism $T_{\lambda_0}\to S$ is of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-finite-fp-locnoeth], so the index $\lambda_0$ of Step 2 satisfies the additional clause.

blueprint_proof_text:
*Step 1: the descended open.* By the finite-approximation tail of
the preceding proof, $N_f=\varprojlim_\lambda T_\lambda$ is a filtered
limit of $S$-schemes with affine transition morphisms, each
$T_\lambda$ being finite over $S$ by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], hence quasi-compact and
quasi-separated; by the recorded input Tag 02LR, applied to the
everywhere quasi-finite morphism $f$ of [pqf-def-quasifinite],
the morphism $\iota_f$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, so
$V:=\iota_f(X)\subset N_f$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme. By
[pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] there are an index $\lambda_1$
and a quasi-compact open $U_{\lambda_1}\subset T_{\lambda_1}$ with
$V=N_f\times_{T_{\lambda_1}}U_{\lambda_1}$; let $U_\lambda$ be the
preimage of $U_{\lambda_1}$ in $T_\lambda$ for
$\lambda\ge\lambda_1$. Clause (3) of the same lemma identifies $V$
with the filtered limit $\varprojlim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_1}U_\lambda$,
the projections being those of $N_f$.

*Step 2: the immersion spreads out.* The morphism $\iota_f$
induces an isomorphism $X\to V$, so $X$ is a closed subscheme of the
limit $\varprojlim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_1}U_\lambda$; the structure
morphism $X\to S$ is locally of finite type by
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and each $U_\lambda$ is
quasi-compact. Hence [pqf-lem-limit-immersion-descends] applies and
the composite $X\to U_\lambda$ is a closed immersion for all
sufficiently large $\lambda$. Fix such an index and call it
$\lambda_0$; enlarging it if necessary we may assume
$\lambda_0\ge\lambda_1$.

*Step 3: factoring the immersion.* The composite
$h:X\to U_{\lambda_0}\hookrightarrow T_{\lambda_0}$ is an immersion,
and it is quasi-compact: for a quasi-compact open
$W\subset T_{\lambda_0}$ the intersection
$U_{\lambda_0}\cap W$ is quasi-compact by
[pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc], since $T_{\lambda_0}$ is
quasi-separated and both $U_{\lambda_0}$ and $W$ are quasi-compact
opens, and $h^{-1}(W)=X\times_{U_{\lambda_0}}(U_{\lambda_0}\cap W)$ is
a closed subscheme of it — the base change of the closed immersion
$X\to U_{\lambda_0}$ — hence is quasi-compact. By the recorded input
Tag 01QV a quasi-compact immersion factors as an open immersion followed
by a closed immersion: there are a scheme $T$, an open immersion
$j:X\to T$ and a closed immersion $i:T\to T_{\lambda_0}$ with
$h=i\circ j$. In that construction $T$ is the closed subscheme of
$T_{\lambda_0}$ whose sheaf of ideals is the kernel of
$\mathcal O_{T_{\lambda_0}}\to h_*\mathcal O_X$, so that $X$ is the
fibre product $T\times_{T_{\lambda_0}}U_{\lambda_0}$ and $j$ is the
base change of the open immersion
$U_{\lambda_0}\hookrightarrow T_{\lambda_0}$ along the closed immersion
$i$; that open immersion is quasi-compact for the same reason as
$h$, and quasi-compactness is stable under base change, so $j$ is a
quasi-compact open immersion, as required.

*Step 4: the finitely presented stage.* If $S$ is
[pqf-def-locnoeth], then the finite morphism
$T_{\lambda_0}\to S$ is of finite presentation by
[pqf-lem-finite-fp-locnoeth], so the index $\lambda_0$ fixed in
Step 2 satisfies the additional clause of the statement.

lean.statement: theorem exists_normalization_immersion_at_finite_stage {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (_hf : f.IsLocallyQuasiFinite) [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (F : f.fromNormalization.FiniteApproximation) : ∃ (l₀ : F.I) (T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (j : X ⟶ T) (i : T ⟶ F.D.obj l₀), IsOpenImmersion j ∧ QuasiCompact j ∧ IsClosedImmersion i ∧ j ≫ i = f.toNormalization ≫ F.π.app l₀ ∧ (IsLocallyNoetherian S → LocallyOfFinitePresentation (F.p l₀))
lean.note: Specializes the existing general finite-approximation immersion theorem to the canonical relative normalization and retains exactly the node’s separated finite-type, everywhere-quasi-finite, and qcqs-base hypotheses. The canonical normalization immersion is a consequence supplied by the normalization-open dependency, not an additional hypothesis. Finite stages are inherent in FiniteApproximation; the last clause uses local finite presentation since finite stages are automatically quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Repair for base 7d675a26 (2026-10-11): upstream moved Scheme.Hom.FiniteApproximation unchanged (same name and fields) from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.ZariskisMainTheorem to WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Integral.FiniteApproximation; the module now imports the latter; statement and declaration unchanged.
